title: Workplace safety training requirements by country: Australia, the EU and Portugal, the US, Japan and the UAE compared
description: How occupational safety training duties compare across Australia, Portugal and the EU, the US, Japan and Abu Dhabi: triggers, refresher cycles and records.
shortAnswer: Workplace safety is the one compliance topic where most of the five markets impose a general training duty on every employer. Australia, the EU, Portugal and Japan all require safety training for each worker, triggered by hiring, job changes or new risks. The United States has no single rule: training duties sit inside individual OSHA standards for specific hazards. In the UAE, the documented framework is emirate level, Abu Dhabi's ADOSH-SF, with risk based training plans reviewed at least annually.
keyTakeaways: General, all employer safety training duties exist in Australia (WHS Act section 19(3)(f)), the EU (Directive 89/391/EEC Article 12), Portugal (Law 102/2009 Article 20) and Japan (Industrial Safety and Health Act Article 59).
The EU and Japan use near identical event triggers: hiring and a change of job in both, plus new equipment and new technology in the EU; Japan adds special education before dangerous or harmful work.

The United States regulates training hazard by hazard: annual for bloodborne pathogens and respiratory protection, eight hours annually for HAZWOPER, three yearly for process safety refreshers and forklift evaluations, event based for hazard communication.
Abu Dhabi's ADOSH-SF is the only framework here that requires a training needs analysis and an annual review of training requirements for nominated entities.
A multinational can standardize event triggers, competence demonstration and record fields, but must localize hazard specific courses, licensed work and local consultation duties.

sections.heading: How do workplace safety training duties compare by market?

blocks.text: Four of the six instruments compared here impose a general duty on every employer, and two take a different route: the United States regulates by hazard, and the UAE coverage in this library is Abu Dhabi's risk classified framework. The table summarizes each as at November 2026.

sections.heading: Which markets impose a general safety training duty on every employer?

blocks.text: Australia, the EU, Portugal and Japan do. Each requires every employer to train each worker for the risks of their job, without first asking whether a specific hazard is present.

Under the model WHS Act, section 19(3)(f) makes necessary information, training, instruction and supervision part of the primary duty of care, and regulation 39 requires training to be suitable and adequate for the nature of the work, the risks at the time and the control measures ([WHS Act duty to train](/regulations/whs-act-duty-to-provide-training)). The EU's Article 12 requires adequate, job specific training for each worker ([EU OSH Framework Directive](/regulations/eu-osh-framework-directive-training)), and Portugal transposes it through Law 102/2009, whose Article 20 adds attention to high risk activities ([Portugal OHS training](/regulations/portugal-ohs-training-requirements)). Japan's Article 59 requires education on hiring and on a change of work, and special education before listed dangerous or harmful operations ([Japan Industrial Safety and Health Act](/regulations/japan-industrial-safety-and-health-act-training)).

The United States is different. OSHA has no single training rule; duties sit inside individual standards and apply only where the hazard exists ([OSHA training requirements](/regulations/osha-training-requirements)). Abu Dhabi's framework requires employers to provide information, instruction, training and supervision in appropriate languages, but the detailed training procedures in Element 5 bind entities nominated by their sector regulator ([Abu Dhabi ADOSH-SF](/regulations/oshad-abu-dhabi-ohs-training)).

sections.heading: How often must safety training be repeated?

blocks.text: Outside the United States, safety training is mostly event based rather than calendar based. The US is the only market where specific standards fix refresher intervals.

items: **EU and Portugal:** training on recruitment, transfer or change of job, new or changed equipment and new technology, repeated periodically if necessary; Portugal adds annual written consultation on the training program.
**Japan:** hiring, a change of work content, and assignment to dangerous or harmful operations; foreman education covers at least 12 hours in designated industries.
**Australia:** no interval; training must keep pace with the risks at the time and the control measures in place.

**United States:** annual for [bloodborne pathogens](/regulations/osha-bloodborne-pathogens-training-requirements) and [respiratory protection](/regulations/osha-respiratory-protection-training-requirements); eight hours annually for [HAZWOPER](/regulations/osha-hazwoper-training-requirements); at least every three years for [process safety management](/regulations/osha-process-safety-management-training-requirements) refreshers and [forklift](/regulations/osha-forklift-operator-training-requirements) evaluations; event based for [hazard communication](/regulations/osha-hazard-communication-training-requirements) and [lockout/tagout](/regulations/osha-lockout-tagout-training-requirements).
**Abu Dhabi:** training requirements reviewed at least annually; Code of Practice 11.0 requires heat training within 10 days of starting employment and before the summer months.

sections.heading: Is attendance enough, or must workers show competence?

blocks.text: Regulators increasingly expect proof of understanding, not attendance. Australia is the most explicit, and the US and Abu Dhabi build verification into specific rules.

Safe Work Australia's model code says it is not sufficient to give a worker a procedure and ask them to acknowledge it. OSHA's process safety rule requires a record of the means used to verify understanding, and its 2010 policy statement requires training in a language and vocabulary workers understand. ADOSH-SF Element 5 requires evaluation of learning outcomes and competency records. Japan's MHLW allows e-learning only where it meets statutory subjects, hours and instructor requirements and confirms attendance.

sections.heading: What should a multinational standardize and what should it localize?

blocks.text: Standardize the event triggers, the competence check and the record schema; localize hazard specific courses, licensed work, consultation duties and heat and climate rules.

blocks.text: Heat is a good example of a topic that must be localized: Abu Dhabi's Code of Practice 11.0 and Japan's heat stroke rules (Ordinance article 612-2, see [Japan heatstroke prevention](/regulations/japan-heatstroke-prevention-obligations)) set their own content and timing. Groups that certify to [ISO 45001](/regulations/iso-45001-competence-and-awareness) often use its competence clause as the common layer, then overlay each market's legal triggers. A [training matrix](/guides/how-to-build-a-training-matrix) keyed to role, site and hazard keeps those overlays auditable.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry structures safety obligations as concepts, roles, hazards and assessment points before content is written, so event triggers and local overlays are explicit and each competence check traces to its legal source. See [operational procedures programs](/programs/operational-procedures).

faqs.q: Does OSHA require annual safety training for all employees?
faqs.a: No. OSHA has no general annual training rule. Annual training is required by specific standards, such as bloodborne pathogens and respiratory protection, and only where the hazard exists. Other standards use three year or event based cycles.

faqs.q: Is the EU Framework Directive enforceable against employers directly?
faqs.a: No. Directive 89/391/EEC binds employers through each Member State's transposing law, so an inspector enforces the national act. In Portugal that is Law 102/2009, which transposes the Directive and adds Portuguese specific duties such as annual consultation on the training program.

faqs.q: Does Abu Dhabi's ADOSH-SF apply across the UAE?
faqs.a: No. It applies in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, and its full training procedures bind entities nominated as high or medium risk by their sector regulator, while Codes of Practice apply to all. This library does not document other emirates' safety frameworks.

faqs.q: Can safety training be delivered by e-learning in Japan?
faqs.a: Yes, within limits. MHLW's e-learning circular, revised September 2, 2026, requires e-learning to meet statutory subjects, hours and instructor requirements and to confirm attendance. Skill training certificates for licensed work cannot be issued digitally.
